newsitem.title: USA: Speaker Gingrich vows to help nation's capital.
newsitem.headline: Speaker Gingrich vows to help nation's capital.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Wednesday Congress should do everything possible to make trouble-plagued Washington the world's finest capital.

"Our dream and our goal for Washington, D.C., should be the finest capital city in the world. And that is so far from where we are today that none of us should take a step back," Gingrich told House Republicans after they renominated him to be speaker for the next two years.

Washington's government is bankrupt and its crime rate is one of the nation's highest. A board created by Congress has taken control of the district's school system, firing the superintendent, and the Washington Post reported that the control board was planning to probe the police department and the University of the District of Columbia.

"We owe it to every child who lives within a few miles of this building to live in a decent neighbourhood, to go to a school that's effective, to be in a drug-free neighbourhood, to have no violence threatening them, to know that their parents can go to work, that they can keep the money they earn, and that there's a future in this capital for every American of every background," Gingrich said.

He did not make any specific proposals. Congress must approve a major portion of Washington's budget because the city is located in the federal enclave of the District of Columbia rather than a state.
